title: Letting AI Formulate the Research Question: Autonomous Research Agents
summary: An AI-agent-run analysis compares annual AlphaEarth/TESSERA reference scores with one-year CONUS tree-cover labels; reference/control corrections did not consistently improve screening, while the supervised classifier scored higher with unequal label resources. The 24 gain positives and partition-sensitive contrasts keep the finding narrow.
ai_technology: The study analyzes learned AlphaEarth/TESSERA annual embeddings and derived scores; the author repository records that AI agents formulated, conducted and wrote the study
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: An AI-agent-run analysis compares annual AlphaEarth/TESSERA reference scores with one-year CONUS tree-cover labels; reference/control corrections did not consistently improve screening, while the supervised classifier scored higher with unequal label resources. The 24 gain positives and partition-sensitive contrasts keep the finding narrow. Evaluation: The source evaluates supplied initial classes on held-out one-year LCMAP pairs (109 gains, 337 losses; 24 gain positives) and a separate Annual NLCD Forest test. It reports unequal label resources for the supervised comparator, reversal of all eight correction contrasts under exploratory partition changes, and limitations against multi-year restoration or ecological-recovery claims.
evidence.unknown: The result is limited to the reported one-year CONUS screening comparison; partition sensitivity and unequal label resources prevent a multi-year restoration or ecological-recovery claim.
